candidates.name: pong-first-event-evidence-v2
candidates.guidance: Judge the first point within the finite horizon, not eventual victory, current paddle quality, or whether this action sounds good. Level 1 is a real outcome: the rally or serve continues without a point through the full horizon. It is NOT a placeholder for uncertainty between winning and losing. Training experience contains many completed no-point windows and losses, with fewer gains; do not assign roughly half the probability to gaining a point without evidence of an opponent miss. Read `observation.objects` and `observation.history`: positive ball vx approaches the RIGHT player, negative vx approaches the LEFT opponent. Wall or paddle bounces can invalidate linear projection; recent direction reversal matters. The candidate lasts only the requested four frames; then the specified controller resumes tracking the ball. Do not extrapolate the candidate motion for the whole horizon. A distant ball often allows the controller to recover; near contact, a small displacement can change the rebound and later outcome. Successful contact is not itself a point. The opponent can return the ball, leaving the window scoreless. Missing ball or opponent does not guarantee a scoreless window: a serve and point may occur before it ends. Use uncertainty when the observations cannot establish the later bounce sequence.
outcome_guidance: Evidence supports the ball passing the RIGHT paddle before any left-side miss. Consider imminent unreachable contact or later failure under the actual continuation. Current misalignment alone is insufficient if there is time to recover.

A complete horizon can contain motion, wall reflections and successful paddle contacts without any point. Treat this as a common distinct event, not a middle rating for an average action. An absent ball alone is not proof that the whole window stays scoreless.

Requires the LEFT opponent actually missing before the player loses, within the horizon. Moving toward or hitting the ball is not scoring. A favorable rebound may produce a gain, but do not infer a guaranteed gain from a locally sensible action.
